newsitem.title: USA: Orlando Utilities sees 355 MW unit up by Sept 7.
newsitem.headline: Orlando Utilities sees 355 MW unit up by Sept 7.

text.p: Orlando Utilities Commission's 355 megawatt (MW) Indian River 3 power unit was expected to resume service by Saturday after being shut Tuesday to repair the unit's boiler insulation, the utility said Thursday.
"It'll be late Friday or Saturday," said utility spokesman Sheridan Beck, when asked for a restart date.
Engineers detected "hot spots" inside the boiler, where parts of the insulation were worn away, and decided to take the unit out of service, Beck said.
The two adjoining units at the Indian River facility were running at full output, he said.
The Indian River complex, near Titusville, Fla., has a total capacity of 619 MW, and uses either fuel oil or natural gas to produce electricity.
